column5: Lots 0 and 1a to 1d-1: PCs, Ethernet cable, internet box, DHCP, terminal, ping and frame capture, desktop switches. Holds the beta fixes and the work shared by several lots.
Lots 1d-2, 1e, 1f and 2a to 2d: cable on the ground, electricity, TCP, Wi-Fi, fixed cabling, peripherals and other home devices. Holds the beta fixes and the work shared by several lots.
Each PC gets its address through a real DHCP exchange with the box and shows it with the state of its lease.
From a computer, ping another computer, which answers: terminal on the tower and the laptop, ip commands, ARP, ICMP.
tcpdump shows the ARP and ICMP frames of a ping; dhclient runs and releases the DHCP lease.
More PCs than the box has ports, all reachable by ping; the port is chosen by aiming at it and the cable leaves from it with its plug.
Cables come down from the ports, lie on the floor and go around walls; the player walks over them.
A device without power is off.
A connection opens between two computers, carries a message and closes.
The laptop connects without a cable.
Cables run through wall sockets and trunking.
A shared file and a network printer.
Phone, camera and TV on the network.
